10 An object X of mass 0.30 kg is travelling in a straight line at a constant velocity of 3.0 m s–1 on a
horizontal frictionless surface. Object X collides with a stationary object Y of mass 0.50 kg.
After the collision, X moves with a velocity of 2.0 m s–1 at an angle of 60 to its direction before the
collision. Object Y moves with a velocity v at an angle of 41 to the direction of X before the
collision, as shown.

hints: Notice the collision is two-dimensional: X leaves at $60^{\circ}$ below the initial line and Y leaves at $41^{\circ}$ above it.
There is zero initial momentum perpendicular to the $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ direction, so the upward $0.50v\sin41^{\circ}$ term must cancel the downward $0.30 \times 2.0\sin60^{\circ}$ term.
Solve $v = (0.30 \times 2.0 \sin60^{\circ})/(0.50 \sin41^{\circ})$ and check it also conserves momentum along the initial direction.
walkthrough: Take the initial direction of X as the x-axis. Initial momentum is only along x: $p_{x}=0.30 \times 3.0 = 0.90\text{ kg m s}^{-1}$, and $p_{y}=0$.
After collision, resolve each momentum into components. For X: $p_{Xx}=0.30 \times 2.0\cos60^{\circ}$ and magnitude of transverse part $p_{Xy}=0.30 \times 2.0\sin60^{\circ}$ downward.
For Y: $p_{Yx}=0.50v\cos41^{\circ}$ and transverse part $p_{Yy}=0.50v\sin41^{\circ}$ upward.
Conservation of momentum perpendicular to the initial motion gives $0 = 0.50v\sin41^{\circ} - 0.30 \times 2.0\sin60^{\circ}$.
Hence $v \approx 1.58\text{ m s}^{-1}$, about $1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$ with correct units. This also conserves x-momentum. This is option C.

A.explanation: Too small because it ignores the vector components and does not balance the $60^{\circ}$ and $41^{\circ}$ transverse momenta.

B.explanation: Too small because it underestimates the transverse momentum of X of mass $0.30\text{ kg}$ at $2.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

C.explanation: Balances momentum perpendicular to the initial direction, giving $0.50v\sin41^{\circ}=0.30 \times 2.0\sin60^{\circ}$ so $v \approx 1.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

D.explanation: Too large and does not satisfy zero total momentum perpendicular to the $3.0\text{ m s}^{-1}$ direction.
